title.zh: 卷一百三十 列傳第五十五 裴陽宋楊崔李解
title.en: Volume 130 Biographies 55: Pei, Yang, Song, , Yang, Cui, Li, Jie
title.raw: 卷一百三十 列傳第五十五 裴陽宋楊崔李解 Volume 130 Biographies 55: Pei, Yang, Song, , Yang, Cui, Li, Jie

sentences.zh: 裴陽宋楊崔李解

translations.literal: Pei, Yang, Song, Yang, Cui, Li, Xie
translations.idiomatic: Pei, Yang, Song, Yang, Cui, Li, and Xie

sentences.zh: ◎裴陽宋楊崔李解

translations.literal: ◎ Pei, Yang, Song, Yang, Cui, Li, Xie
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Biographies of Pei, Yang, Song, Yang, Cui, Li, and Xie

sentences.zh: 裴漼，絳州聞喜著姓。

translations.literal: Pei Hui was of the prominent Pei clan of Wenxi in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Hui belonged to the eminent Pei lineage of Wenxi in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父琰之，永徽中為同州司戶參軍，年甚少，不主曹務，刺史李崇義內輕之，鐫諭曰：「同，三輔，吏事繁，子盍求便官？

translations.literal: His father Yan Zhi, in the Yonghui era served as Tongzhou Registrar, was very young, did not attend to bureau duties, and Prefect Li Chongyi inwardly looked down on him and engraved an admonition saying: "Tong is one of the Three Metropolises; official business is heavy—why do you not seek a convenient post?
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan Zhi served as registrar of Tong Prefecture during the Yonghui reign. He was still very young and neglected his bureau duties. Prefect Li Chongyi privately despised him and had an inscription carved that read: "Tong is one of the three metropolitan circuits, and its paperwork is overwhelming. Why not seek a more comfortable appointment?

sentences.zh: 毋留此！」

translations.literal: Do not remain here!"
translations.idiomatic: Do not stay here!"

sentences.zh: 琰之唯唯。

translations.literal: Yan Zhi assented repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhi could only murmur his assent.

sentences.zh: 吏白積案數百，崇義讓使趣斷，琰之曰：「何至逼人？」

translations.literal: A clerk reported that several hundred cases had piled up; Chongyi reproached him and ordered him to hurry and decide them. Yan Zhi said: "Why go so far as to press people?"
translations.idiomatic: When a clerk reported that several hundred cases had accumulated, Chongyi rebuked him and ordered him to dispose of them quickly. Yan Zhi said, "Why drive people so hard?"

sentences.zh: 乃命吏連紙進筆為省決，一日畢，既與奪當理，而筆詞勁妙。

translations.literal: He then ordered clerks to join sheets of paper and bring brushes forward to decide cases in summary; in one day he finished, and both the judgments and the reasoning were correct, while his phrasing was forceful and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: He then had clerks string sheets of paper together, handed him a brush, and settled every case in summary fashion in a single day. His rulings were legally sound, and his prose was vigorous and polished.

sentences.zh: 崇義驚曰：「子何自晦，成吾過耶？」

translations.literal: Chongyi said in astonishment: "Why did you hide your talent and make me at fault?"
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi exclaimed in astonishment, "Why did you conceal your abilities and make me look foolish?"

sentences.zh: 由是名動一州，號「霹靂手」。

translations.literal: From this his fame shook the whole prefecture, and he was called the "Thunderbolt Hand."
translations.idiomatic: From that day his reputation resounded through the prefecture, and men called him the Thunderbolt Hand.

sentences.zh: 後為永年令，有惠政，吏刻石頌美。

translations.literal: Later he became magistrate of Yongnian, had benevolent administration, and clerks carved stone to praise his excellence.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as magistrate of Yongnian, where his benevolent rule led the clerks to carve a stone inscription in his praise.

sentences.zh: 以倉部郎中病廢。

translations.literal: As Director of the Granary Bureau he fell ill and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was forced to retire on account of illness while serving as director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 漼侍疾十餘年，不肯仕。

translations.literal: Hui attended his illness for more than ten years and refused to take office.
translations.idiomatic: Hui nursed him for more than ten years and refused to enter government service.

sentences.zh: 琰之沒，始擢明經，調陳留主簿，遷監察御史。

translations.literal: When Yan Zhi died, he was first selected through the Mingjing examination, appointed Chenliu Registrar, and promoted to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Yan Zhi's death did Hui pass the Mingjing examination, receive appointment as registrar of Chenliu, and rise to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 時崔湜、鄭愔典吏部，坐奸贓，為李尚隱所劾，詔漼按訊，而安樂公主、上官昭容為阿右，漼執正其罪，天下稱之。

translations.literal: At that time Cui Shi and Zheng Yin controlled the Ministry of Personnel and were implicated in corruption; they were impeached by Li Shangyin. An edict ordered Hui to investigate. Princess Anle and Shangguan Zhaorong shielded them, but Hui upheld their guilt, and the realm praised him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Cui Shi and Zheng Yin ran the Ministry of Personnel and were caught in bribery and graft. Li Shangyin impeached them, and the throne ordered Hui to conduct the inquiry. Princess Anle and Shangguan Zhaorong tried to protect them, but Hui stood firm and secured their conviction, winning acclaim throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 累進中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to drafting attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 睿宗造金仙、玉真二觀，時旱甚，役不止，漼上言：「春夏毋聚大眾，起大役，不可興土功，妨農事。

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong built the Jinxian and Yuzhen monasteries. The drought was severe and corvée labor did not cease. Hui submitted a memorial: "In spring and summer one must not gather great crowds or launch great projects; one must not undertake earthworks and hinder agricultural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong was building the Jinxian and Yuzhen monasteries. The drought was severe, yet labor levies never stopped. Hui memorialized the throne: "In spring and summer the state must not gather huge crowds or launch great public works, nor undertake construction that interferes with farming.

sentences.zh: 若役使乖度，則有疾疫水旱之災，此天人常應也。

translations.literal: If labor service violates proper measure, then there will be pestilence and flood-and-drought disasters—this is the constant correspondence between Heaven and man.
translations.idiomatic: When corvée service exceeds proper bounds, pestilence and flood-or-drought calamities follow. That is the constant correspondence between Heaven and humanity.

sentences.zh: 今自冬徂春，雨不時降，人心憔然，莫知所出，而土木方興，時暵之孽，職為此發。

translations.literal: Now from winter into spring rain has not fallen in season; people's hearts are haggard and they do not know what to do, yet construction is just rising—the seasonal drought is chiefly caused by this.
translations.idiomatic: From winter into spring the rains have not come in season. The people are worn down and do not know which way to turn, yet building projects are only now expanding. The present drought stems chiefly from this.

sentences.zh: 今東作雲始，丁壯就功，妨多益少，饑寒有漸。

translations.literal: Now the eastern plowing is just beginning and able-bodied men go to labor service—harm is great and benefit small; hunger and cold are gradually approaching.
translations.idiomatic: Spring planting is just beginning, yet able-bodied men are being pulled into construction work. The harm far outweighs the gain, and hunger and cold are drawing near.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》莊公三十一年冬，不雨，是時歲三築臺；

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals records that in the thirty-first year of Duke Zhuang, winter, there was no rain—at that time towers were built three times in the year;
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals notes that in the thirty-first year of Duke Zhuang, winter brought no rain while three towers were built that same year;

sentences.zh: 僖公二十一年夏，大旱，是時作南門。

translations.literal: in the twenty-first year of Duke Xi, summer, there was great drought—at that time the south gate was being built.
translations.idiomatic: and in the twenty-first year of Duke Xi a great summer drought coincided with construction of the south gate.

sentences.zh: 陛下以四方為念，宜下明制，令二京營作、和市木石，一切停止。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, with the four quarters in mind, should issue a clear regulation ordering that construction in the two capitals and the market purchase of timber and stone all cease entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, bearing the four quarters in mind, should issue a clear edict halting all construction in the two capitals and all government purchases of timber and stone.

sentences.zh: 有如農桑失時，戶口流散，雖寺觀營立，能救饑寒敝哉！」

translations.literal: If farming and sericulture miss their season and households disperse, even if temples and monasteries are built, can they rescue hunger, cold, and destitution!"
translations.idiomatic: If farming and sericulture miss their season and the population scatters, what good will finished temples and monasteries do against hunger, cold, and ruin?"

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 以銓總勞，特授一子官。

translations.literal: Because of the overall labor of personnel selection, one son was specially granted an office.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of his exhaustive work in personnel selection, one of his sons was specially granted an official post.

sentences.zh: 開元五年，為吏部侍郎，甄拔士為多。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan he became Vice Minister of Personnel and selected and promoted many scholars.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 5 he became vice minister of personnel and recommended a great many worthy men.

sentences.zh: 拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 漼雅與張說善，說方宰相，數薦之，漼長於敷奏，天子亦自重焉，擢吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Hui had long been on good terms with Zhang Yue. Yue was then chief minister and repeatedly recommended him. Hui excelled at memorials and presentations, and the Son of Heaven also valued him highly, promoting him to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had long been close to Zhang Yue, who was then chief minister and repeatedly recommended him. Hui excelled at memorials and court presentations, and the emperor held him in high regard as well, elevating him to minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 世儉素，而晚節稍畜伎妾，為奢侈事，議者以為缺。

translations.literal: All his life he was frugal and plain, but in his later years he gradually kept singing girls and concubines and engaged in extravagant affairs; critics regarded this as a flaw.
translations.idiomatic: He had lived frugally all his life, but in his later years he began keeping entertainers and concubines and indulging in luxury, which critics counted against him.

sentences.zh: 改太子賓客。

translations.literal: He was changed to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈禮部尚書，謚曰懿。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Rites, with the posthumous title Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as minister of rites, with the posthumous title Yi.

sentences.zh: 從祖弟寬。

translations.literal: His younger cousin by a collateral line was Kuan.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin Kuan is treated next.

sentences.zh: 寬，性通敏，工騎射、彈棋、投壺，略通書記。

translations.literal: Kuan was by nature quick and perceptive, skilled at mounted archery, pitch-pot, and ball-toss, and had some knowledge of documents.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan was quick-witted by nature, skilled in horsemanship, archery, pitch-pot, and ball tossing, and had a modest command of written records.

sentences.zh: 景雲中，為潤州參軍事。

translations.literal: In the Jingyun era he was an aide in Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyun reign he served as aide in Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 刺史韋詵有女，擇所宜歸，會休日登樓，見人於後圃有所瘞藏者，訪諸吏，曰：「參軍裴寬居也。」

translations.literal: Prefect Wei Shen had a daughter and was choosing a suitable husband. On a rest day he went up a tower and saw someone in the rear garden burying something. He asked the clerks, who said: "That is where Military Aide Pei Kuan lives."
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Wei Shen had a daughter and was looking for a suitable husband. On a holiday he climbed a tower and saw someone in the rear garden burying something. When he asked the clerks, they said, "That is Military Aide Pei Kuan's residence."

sentences.zh: 與偕來，詵問狀，答曰：「寬義不以包苴汙家，適有人以鹿為餉，致而去，不敢自欺，故瘞之。」

translations.literal: He went with him to visit. Shen asked the circumstances, and Kuan answered: "In righteousness Kuan would not let bribes stain the household. Just then someone had presented a deer as a gift; I received it and he left. I dared not deceive myself, so I buried it."
translations.idiomatic: He went with them to investigate. Shen asked what had happened, and Kuan replied, "I would never let gifts corrupt my household. Someone had just offered me a deer; I accepted it, he left, and I could not deceive myself, so I buried it."

sentences.zh: 詵嗟異，乃引為按察判官，許妻以女。

translations.literal: Shen sighed in admiration, then brought him in as an investigation commissioner aide and promised him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Shen marveled and took him on as aide to the investigation commissioner, promising him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 歸語妻曰：「常求佳婿，今得矣。」

translations.literal: Returning home he told his wife: "I have long sought a fine son-in-law; now I have found one."
translations.idiomatic: When he returned home he told his wife, "I have long sought a fine son-in-law, and now I have found one."

sentences.zh: 明日，幃其族使觀之。

translations.literal: The next day he screened off his clansmen and had them observe him.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he had his clansmen observe him from behind a screen.

sentences.zh: 寬時衣碧，瘠而長，既入，族人皆笑，呼為「碧鸛雀」。

translations.literal: Kuan was then dressed in green, thin and tall. Once he entered, the clansmen all laughed and called him the "Green Stork."
translations.idiomatic: Kuan was wearing green, thin and very tall. When he entered, the clansmen all laughed and called him the Green Stork.

sentences.zh: 詵曰：「愛其女，必以為賢公侯妻也，何可以貌求人？」

translations.literal: Shen said: "Because I love my daughter, I must take her for the wife of a worthy marquis or duke—how can one seek a man by appearance?"
translations.idiomatic: Shen said, "Because I love my daughter, I mean to give her to a worthy man fit to become a great noble. How can one judge a husband by looks alone?"

sentences.zh: 卒妻寬。

translations.literal: In the end he gave his daughter to Kuan in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he married his daughter to Kuan.

sentences.zh: 舉拔萃，為河南丞，遷長安尉。

translations.literal: He passed the Bacui examination, became Henan Assistant Magistrate, and was transferred to Chang'an Sheriff.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the exceptional-talent examination, served as assistant magistrate of Henan, and was promoted to sheriff of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 宇文融為侍御史，括天下田，奏為江東覆田判官。

translations.literal: Yuwen Rong was Attending Censor and surveyed land throughout the realm; he memorialized to make Kuan an aide for land re-survey in Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Rong, as attending censor, undertook a nationwide land survey, he had Kuan appointed aide for the Jiangdong re-survey.

sentences.zh: 改太常博士。

translations.literal: He was changed to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 禮部建言忌日享廟應用樂，寬自以情立議曰：「廟尊忌卑則作樂，廟卑忌尊則備而不奏。」

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites proposed that music should be used when offering at the temple on the anniversary of death. Kuan, judging by principle, set forth an opinion: "When the temple is higher in rank and the anniversary lower, then make music; when the temple is lower in rank and the anniversary higher, then prepare but do not perform."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites proposed using music when offering at the ancestral temple on a death anniversary. Kuan argued from principle: "When the temple outranks the anniversary observance, music may be performed; when the anniversary outranks the temple, instruments may be prepared but not played."

sentences.zh: 中書令張說善之，請如寬議。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Yue approved it and requested that Kuan's opinion be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Yue approved and asked that Kuan's proposal be adopted.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 萬騎將軍馬崇白日殺人，而王毛仲方以貴幸，將鬻其獄，寬固執不肯從。

translations.literal: General of Ten Thousand Riders Ma Chong killed a man in broad daylight, and Wang Maozhong was then in favor and was about to sell the case; Kuan firmly held to the law and refused to comply.
translations.idiomatic: General Ma Chong of the Ten Thousand Riders murdered a man in broad daylight. Wang Maozhong, then in imperial favor, tried to buy off the case, but Kuan held to the law and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 河西節度使蕭嵩表為判官，歷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Hexi Military Commissioner Xiao Song memorialized him as an aide and he served through Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi military commissioner Xiao Song recommended him as aide, and he rose to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 宰相裴耀卿領江淮運，列倉河陰，奏寬為戶部侍郎自副。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Pei Yaojing oversaw Jiang-Huai transport, established granaries at Heyin, and memorialized to make Kuan Vice Minister of Revenue as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Pei Yaojing directed Jiang-Huai transport and established granaries at Heyin; he had Kuan appointed vice minister of revenue as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 出為蒲州刺史，州久旱，寬入境輒雨。

translations.literal: He went out as Prefect of Pu; the prefecture had long been in drought, and when Kuan entered the border rain fell at once.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Pu. The prefecture had suffered a long drought, but rain fell as soon as Kuan crossed the border.

sentences.zh: 徙河南尹，不屈附權貴，河南大治。

translations.literal: He was moved to Metropolitan Governor of Henan, would not bend to attach himself to the powerful, and Henan was greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to metropolitan governor of Henan, refused to truckle to the powerful, and brought the capital district under excellent order.

sentences.zh: 由金吾大將軍授太原尹，玄宗賦詩褒餞。

translations.literal: From General of the Golden Crow Guards he was appointed Metropolitan Governor of Taiyuan; Emperor Xuanzong composed a poem to praise and send him off.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as general of the Golden Crow Guards he was appointed metropolitan governor of Taiyuan, and Emperor Xuanzong wrote a poem to honor his departure.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，由陳留太守拜范陽節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, from Administrator of Chenliu he was appointed Fanyang Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao reign he rose from administrator of Chenliu to military commissioner of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 時北平軍使烏承恩，虜酋也，與中人通，數冒賄，寬以法繩治。

translations.literal: At that time the Beiping army commissioner Wu Cheng'en was a barbarian chieftain who colluded with eunuchs and repeatedly took bribes; Kuan punished him according to law.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Beiping army commissioner Wu Cheng'en, a tribal leader, colluded with eunuchs and repeatedly accepted bribes; Kuan punished him by law.

sentences.zh: 檀州刺史何僧獻生口數十，寬悉歸之，故夷夏感附。

translations.literal: Tan Prefecture Prefect He Sengxian presented several dozen captives; Kuan returned them all, and therefore both barbarians and Chinese were moved to attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Prefecture prefect He Sengxian presented several dozen captives; Kuan returned them all, winning the heartfelt loyalty of both Chinese and non-Chinese subjects.

sentences.zh: 三載，用安祿山守范陽，召寬為戶部尚書，兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the third year An Lushan was used to guard Fanyang; Kuan was summoned as Minister of Revenue and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianbao, An Lushan was put in charge of Fanyang, and Kuan was recalled as minister of revenue and concurrent censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 裴敦復平海賊還，廣張功簿，寬密白其妄。

translations.literal: Pei Dunfu returned after pacifying sea bandits and widely inflated his record of merit; Kuan secretly reported that it was false.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Dunfu returned from suppressing pirates at sea, he greatly inflated his merit rolls; Kuan secretly reported the exaggeration to the throne.

sentences.zh: 會河北部將入朝，盛譽寬政，且言華虜猶思之，帝嗟賞，眷倚加厚。

translations.literal: It happened that Hebei generals entered court and lavishly praised Kuan's administration, saying that both Chinese and barbarians still longed for him. The Emperor sighed in admiration and his favor and reliance grew heavier.
translations.idiomatic: When generals from Hebei arrived at court, they lavishly praised Kuan's governance and said that Chinese and non-Chinese alike still missed him. The emperor marveled and leaned on him all the more.

sentences.zh: 李林甫恐其遂相，又惡寬善李適之，乃漏寬語以激敦復，敦復任氣而疏，以林甫為誠。

translations.literal: Li Linfu feared that he would become chief minister and also hated that Kuan was friendly with Li Shizhi, so he leaked Kuan's words to provoke Dunfu. Dunfu was headstrong and unsuspecting and regarded Linfu as sincere.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu feared that Kuan might become chief minister and resented his friendship with Li Shizhi, so he leaked Kuan's remarks to provoke Pei Dunfu. Dunfu was impulsive and unsuspecting, and took Linfu at his word.

sentences.zh: 先是，寬以所善請於敦復，即欲白髮其言，林甫趣之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Kuan had asked a favor of Dunfu through someone he trusted and was about to report Dunfu's words to the throne; Linfu urged him on.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Kuan had asked a favor of Dunfu through a trusted intermediary and was about to expose Dunfu's indiscretion; Linfu spurred him on.

sentences.zh: 敦復未及聞，扈幸溫泉宮。

translations.literal: Dunfu had not yet heard when he accompanied the Emperor to Huaqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before Dunfu learned of it, the court moved to Huaqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 而其下裨將程藏曜、曹鑒自以他事系臺，寬捕按之，敦復謂寬求致其罪，遽以金五百兩賂貴妃姊，因得事聞於帝，由是貶寬睢陽太守。

translations.literal: His subordinate staff generals Cheng Zangyao and Cao Jian had been detained at the censorate on other matters; Kuan arrested and investigated them. Dunfu thought Kuan was seeking to bring them to guilt, and hastily bribed the Consort's elder sister with five hundred taels of gold, thereby getting the matter reported to the Emperor. For this Kuan was demoted to Administrator of Suiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Two of his subordinate generals, Cheng Zangyao and Cao Jian, had been detained by the censorate on other charges, and Kuan pursued the case. Dunfu believed Kuan was trying to frame them and quickly bribed the elder sister of the imperial consort with five hundred taels of gold, bringing the matter before the emperor. Kuan was demoted to administrator of Suiyang.

sentences.zh: 及韋堅獄起，寬復坐親，貶安陸別駕。

translations.literal: When the Wei Jian case arose, Kuan was again implicated through kinship and demoted to Vice Administrator of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei Jian affair broke, Kuan was implicated again through family ties and demoted to vice administrator of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 林甫任羅希奭殺李適之也，亦使過安陸，將怖殺寬，寬叩頭祈哀，希奭乃去。

translations.literal: Linfu had entrusted Luo Xi'ao to kill Li Shizhi and also sent him through Anlu intending to frighten Kuan to death; Kuan knocked his head and begged for mercy, and Xi'ao then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu had sent Luo Xi'ao to kill Li Shizhi and also sent him through Anlu intending to terrorize Kuan to death. Kuan kowtowed and pleaded for his life, and Xi'ao left him alone.

sentences.zh: 寬懼終見殺，丐為浮屠，不許。

translations.literal: Kuan feared he would ultimately be killed and begged to become a Buddhist monk; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he would still be killed, Kuan asked to become a monk, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 稍遷東海太守，徙馮翊，入為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to Administrator of Donghai, moved to Fengyi, and entered court as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to administrator of Donghai, transferred to Fengyi, and recalled to serve as minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十五，贈太子太傅。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-five and was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-five and was posthumously honored as grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 寬兄弟八人，皆擢明經，任臺、省、州刺史。

translations.literal: Kuan had eight brothers, all selected through the Mingjing examination, serving in the censorate, secretariat ministries, and as prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan had eight brothers, all of whom passed the Mingjing examination and held posts in the censorate, central ministries, or as prefects.

sentences.zh: 雅性友愛，於東都治第，八院相對，甥侄亦有名稱，常擊鼓會飯。

translations.literal: He was by nature fond of brotherly affection; at the Eastern Capital he built a mansion with eight courtyards facing one another. His nephews and sons-in-law also had reputation, and they often beat drums to gather for meals.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to his kin and built a mansion in the Eastern Capital with eight courtyards facing one another. His nephews and sons-in-law were well known as well, and the family often beat drums to summon one another to shared meals.

sentences.zh: 其為政務清簡，所蒞人愛之，世皆冀其得宰相。

translations.literal: In governing he strove for clarity and simplicity; wherever he served the people loved him, and the age all hoped he would attain the chief ministership.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was clear and unpretentious, and the people wherever he served loved him. All his contemporaries hoped he would become chief minister.

sentences.zh: 天寶間稱舊德，以寬為首。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era they spoke of old virtue, with Kuan at the head.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao reign he was regarded as foremost among men of established virtue.

sentences.zh: 然惑於佛，喜與桑門遊，習誦其書，老彌篤雲。

translations.literal: Yet he was deluded by Buddhism, delighted to roam with monks, practiced reciting their scriptures, and grew all the more earnest in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was drawn to Buddhism, delighted in the company of monks, memorized their scriptures, and grew only more devout with age.

sentences.zh: 子谞。

translations.literal: His son Xu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xu is treated next.

sentences.zh: 谞，字士明，擢明經，調河南參軍事。

translations.literal: Xu, style name Shiming, was selected through the Mingjing examination and appointed Henan Military Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Xu, whose style was Shiming, passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed military aide in Henan.

sentences.zh: 性通綽，舉止不煩。

translations.literal: His nature was broad and easy; in conduct he was unburdened.
translations.idiomatic: He was broad-minded by nature and unassuming in manner.

sentences.zh: 累遷京兆倉曹參軍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Jingzhao Granary Bureau Aide.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to granary bureau aide in the metropolitan prefecture of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 虢王巨表署襄、鄧營田判官。

translations.literal: Prince of Guo Ju memorialized him as an aide for garrison-farming in Xiang and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Guo Ju recommended him as aide for garrison-farming in Xiang and Deng.

sentences.zh: 母喪，居東都。

translations.literal: When his mother died he resided at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he remained in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 會史思明亂，逃山谷間。

translations.literal: It happened that Shi Siming rebelled, and he fled among mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming rebelled, he fled into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 思明故為寬將，德寬舊恩，且聞谞名，遣捕騎跡獲之，喜甚，呼為「郎君」，偽授御史中丞。

translations.literal: Siming had formerly been Kuan's subordinate general, owed Kuan old kindness, and had also heard of Xu's reputation. He sent pursuing riders who tracked and captured him, was greatly pleased, called him "Young Master," and falsely appointed him Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Siming had once served under Kuan and still honored his old patronage; he had also heard of Xu's reputation. He sent riders who tracked Xu down, was delighted, called him Young Master, and gave him the false title of vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 賊殘殺宗室，谞陰緩之。

translations.literal: The rebels brutally killed members of the imperial clan; Xu secretly slowed the killing.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels slaughtered members of the imperial clan, Xu secretly slowed the killing.

sentences.zh: 全活者數百人。

translations.literal: Those wholly preserved alive numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred people were thereby saved.

sentences.zh: 又嘗疏賊虛實於朝，事泄，思明恨罵，危死而免。

translations.literal: He also once sent a memorial to court on the rebels' true and false strength; the matter leaked, Siming cursed him in hatred, and he narrowly escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: He also once sent intelligence on the rebels' strength to the court. When the report was discovered, Siming raged at him and he narrowly escaped death.

sentences.zh: 賊平，除太子中允，遷考功郎中，數燕見奏事。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified he was made Palace Companion to the Heir Apparent, transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel for merit evaluation, and repeatedly received informal audiences to report affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed he was appointed companion to the heir apparent, promoted to director in the Ministry of Personnel, and repeatedly received informal audiences to report on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 代宗幸陜，谞徒步挾考功南曹印赴行在，帝曰：「疾風知勁草，果可信。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong went to Shan, Xu went on foot carrying the seal of the southern bureau of merit evaluation to the traveling court. The Emperor said: "A fierce wind reveals the tough grass—he is truly trustworthy."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong went to Shan, Xu walked on foot carrying the seal of the southern bureau of merit evaluation to the traveling court. The emperor said, "A fierce wind reveals the tough grass—he is truly trustworthy."

sentences.zh: 將用為御史中丞，為元載沮卻，故拜河東租庸、鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: He was about to be used as Vice Censor-in-Chief, but Yuan Zai obstructed and blocked it, so he was appointed Commissioner for Zuoyong and Salt and Iron in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to be made vice censor-in-chief, but Yuan Zai blocked the appointment, so he was made commissioner for zuoyong levies and salt and iron in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 時關輔旱，谞入計，帝召至便殿，問榷酤利歲出內幾何，谞久不對。

translations.literal: At that time Guanfu was in drought. Xu entered to render accounts; the Emperor summoned him to the side hall and asked how much profit from the monopoly on wine entered the inner palace each year. Xu long did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The capital region was suffering drought. When Xu came to render accounts, the emperor summoned him to a side hall and asked how much profit from the wine monopoly reached the inner palace each year. Xu remained silent for a long time.

sentences.zh: 帝復問，曰：「臣有所思。」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked again, and he said: "Your servant has something on his mind."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked again, and Xu said, "Your servant has been thinking."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「何邪？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "What is it?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "About what?"

sentences.zh: 谞曰：「臣自河東來，涉三百里，而農人愁嘆，谷菽未種。

translations.literal: Xu said: "Your servant came from Hedong, traveling three hundred li, and the farmers were sighing in distress; grain and beans had not yet been planted.
translations.idiomatic: Xu said, "Coming from Hedong I traveled three hundred li and saw farmers sighing in distress, with grain and beans still unplanted.

sentences.zh: 誠謂陛下軫念元元，先訪疾苦，而乃責臣以利。

translations.literal: I truly thought Your Majesty would be concerned for the common people and first inquire about their suffering and hardship, yet instead you charged your servant about profit.
translations.idiomatic: I truly believed Your Majesty would care for the common people and ask first about their hardships, yet Your Majesty questioned me about profit.

sentences.zh: 孟子曰：『治國者，仁義而已，何以利為？』

translations.literal: Mencius said: 'He who governs the state needs only benevolence and righteousness—why take profit as the aim?
translations.idiomatic: Mencius said, 'To govern a state requires only benevolence and righteousness—why make profit the goal?

sentences.zh: 故未敢即對。」

translations.literal: Therefore I did not dare answer at once."
translations.idiomatic: That is why I did not dare answer immediately."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「微公言，朕不聞此。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "But for your words, I would not have heard this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "But for your words, I would never have heard this."

sentences.zh: 拜左司郎中，數訪政事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Department Director and repeatedly consulted on government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director of the left department and was repeatedly consulted on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 載忌之，出為虔州刺史，歷饒、廬、亳三州，除右金吾將軍。

translations.literal: Zai resented him and sent him out as Prefect of Qian, then through Rao, Lu, and Bo prefectures, and finally appointed Right General of the Golden Crow Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Zai resented him and sent him out as prefect of Qian, then through Rao, Lu, and Bo, before appointing him right general of the Golden Crow Guards.

sentences.zh: 德宗新即位，以刑名治天下，百吏震服。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong had newly ascended, he governed the realm through penal law and nomenclature, and all officials trembled in submission.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong had just ascended the throne, he governed the realm through strict penal law, and every official trembled before him.

sentences.zh: 時大行將蕆陵事，禁屠殺，尚父郭子儀家奴宰羊，谞列奏，帝謂不畏強禦，善之，或曰：「尚父有社稷功，豈不為庇之？」

translations.literal: At that time the late emperor's burial was about to be completed and slaughter was forbidden. The Senior Mentor Guo Ziyi's household slave slaughtered a sheep; Xu memorialized it in detail. The Emperor said he did not fear the powerful and approved him. Someone said: "The Senior Mentor has merit for the altars of state—should you not shield him?"
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor's burial was nearing completion and slaughter was forbidden. Senior Mentor Guo Ziyi's household slave butchered a sheep, and Xu reported it in full. The emperor praised him for not fearing the powerful. Someone asked, "The Senior Mentor saved the dynasty—should you not shield him?"

sentences.zh: 谞笑曰：「非君所知。

translations.literal: Xu laughed and said: "This is not something you understand.
translations.idiomatic: Xu smiled and said, "That is not how you should see it.

sentences.zh: 尚父方貴盛，上新即位，必謂黨附者眾。

translations.literal: The Senior Mentor is at the height of honor and power, and the new emperor has just taken the throne—he is sure to think that those who attach themselves to him are many.
translations.idiomatic: The Senior Mentor is at the height of his power, and a new emperor has just taken the throne. He is sure to think that many men are flocking to his faction.

sentences.zh: 今發其細過，以明不恃權耳。

translations.literal: Now by exposing his small fault I make clear that he does not rely on power.
translations.idiomatic: By exposing this small fault now, I show that he does not rely on power alone.

sentences.zh: 吾上以盡事君之道，下以安大臣，不亦可乎？」

translations.literal: Above I thereby fulfill the way of serving the ruler; below I thereby reassure great ministers—is this not fitting?"
translations.idiomatic: Above, I fulfill my duty to the ruler; below, I reassure a great minister. Is that not fitting?"

sentences.zh: 時朝堂別置三司決庶獄，辨爭者輒擊登聞鼓。

translations.literal: At that time the court separately established three offices to decide common cases, and those in dispute would strike the Petition-to-the-Throne drum.
translations.idiomatic: The court had set up three special offices to decide ordinary cases, and litigants would strike the Petition-to-the-Throne drum at will.

sentences.zh: 谞上疏曰：「諫鼓、謗木之設，所以達幽枉，延直言。

translations.literal: Xu submitted a memorial: "The remonstrance drum and the slander post were established in order to reach hidden wrongs and extend forthright speech.
translations.idiomatic: Xu memorialized: "The remonstrance drum and the criticism post were established to reach hidden wrongs and encourage frank speech.

sentences.zh: 今詭猾之人，輕動天聽，爭纖微，若然者，安用吏治乎？」

translations.literal: Now crafty and slippery men lightly move the imperial ear and wrangle over trifles—if it is like this, what use is there for officials to govern?"
translations.idiomatic: Now crafty men lightly disturb the imperial ear over trifles. If that continues, what need is there for regular official governance?"

sentences.zh: 帝然之，於是悉歸有司。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved it, and thereupon all cases were returned to the regular offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and all such cases were returned to the regular offices.

sentences.zh: 谞惡法吏舞文，或挾宿怨為重輕，因獻《獄官箴》以諷。

translations.literal: Xu hated legal clerks who twisted the statutes or, bearing old resentments, made punishments heavy or light; he therefore presented the Admonition for Prison Officials as satire.
translations.idiomatic: Xu detested legal clerks who twisted statutes or let old grudges dictate sentences, and he presented the Admonition for Prison Officials as a pointed warning.

sentences.zh: 坐所善誅，貶閬州司馬。

translations.literal: Because someone he favored was executed, he was demoted to Lang Prefecture Vice Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Because a man he favored was executed, he was demoted to vice administrator of Lang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 俄召為太子右庶子，進兵部侍郎，至河南尹、東都副留守。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Right Companion to the Heir Apparent, advanced to Vice Minister of War, and reached Metropolitan Governor of Henan and Deputy Protector of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as right companion to the heir apparent, rose to vice minister of war, and became metropolitan governor of Henan and deputy protector of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 凡五世為河南，谞視事未嘗敢當正處。

translations.literal: For five generations his family had served in Henan; when Xu took office he never dared occupy the central seat.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations of his family had served in Henan, and when Xu took office he never dared sit in the central seat.

sentences.zh: 以寬厚和易為治，不鞫人以贓。

translations.literal: He governed with generosity, kindness, and ease, and did not interrogate people for corruption.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with generosity and ease and did not hound people on corruption charges.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十五，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-five and was posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-five and was posthumously honored as minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 寬弟子胄，字胤叔，擢明經，佐李抱玉鳳翔幕府。

translations.literal: Kuan's nephew Zhou, style name Yinshu, was selected through the Mingjing examination and assisted Li Baoyu in the Fengxiang headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan's nephew Zhou, styled Yinshu, passed the Mingjing examination and served on Li Baoyu's staff at Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 不得意，謝歸，更從宣歙觀察使陳少遊，抱玉怒，劾貶桐廬尉。

translations.literal: Dissatisfied, he resigned and returned, then followed Xuanshe Observation Commissioner Chen Shaoyou. Baoyu was angry and impeached him, demoting him to Tonglu Sheriff.
translations.idiomatic: Unhappy in the post, he resigned and later joined the staff of Xuanshe observation commissioner Chen Shaoyou. Baoyu was furious and had him impeached and demoted to sheriff of Tonglu.

sentences.zh: 時李棲筠觀察浙西，幕府皆一時高選。

translations.literal: At that time Li Qiyun observed Zhexi, and his staff were all eminent selections of the age.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Qiyun was observation commissioner of Zhexi, and his staff were all eminent men of the day.

sentences.zh: 判官許鳴謙名知人，見崔造及胄，器之，白棲筠取胄為支使。

translations.literal: Aide Xu Mingqian was famed for knowing men; seeing Cui Zao and Zhou, he valued them and told Qiyun to take Zhou as branch commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Aide Xu Mingqian was famed for judging talent. Seeing Cui Zao and Zhou, he valued them and urged Qiyun to appoint Zhou as branch commissioner.

sentences.zh: 代宗惡宰相元載怙權，召棲筠為御史大夫，欲以相，棲筠引胄殿中侍御史，尤為載所惡。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong hated Chief Minister Yuan Zai's grasp on power, summoned Qiyun as Censor-in-Chief intending to make him chief minister, and Qiyun brought in Zhou as Palace Attending Censor—especially hated by Zai.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong hated chief minister Yuan Zai's monopoly on power, recalled Qiyun as censor-in-chief intending to make him chief minister, and Qiyun brought Zhou in as palace attending censor, which Zai especially resented.

sentences.zh: 會棲筠卒，胄護喪歸洛陽，人為危之，胄屹然不沮惴。

translations.literal: It happened that Qiyun died; Zhou escorted the coffin back to Luoyang. People regarded him as in danger, but Zhou stood firm without dismay or fear.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiyun died, Zhou escorted the coffin to Luoyang. Others thought him in grave danger, but he remained unshaken.

sentences.zh: 少遊復表為淮南觀察判官。

translations.literal: Shaoyou again memorialized to make him Huainan Observation Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shaoyou again recommended him as observation aide in Huainan.

sentences.zh: 載誅，始拜刑部員外郎，遷宣州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zai was executed, he was first appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice and transferred to Prefect of Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Zai was executed, Zhou was appointed vice director in the Ministry of Justice and then prefect of Xuan.

sentences.zh: 楊炎當國，為載復仇，窮摭所惡。

translations.literal: Yang Yan held the state, avenging Zai, and exhaustively seized upon those he hated.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yan dominated the government, he avenged Zai and hunted down everyone he hated.

sentences.zh: 會胄部人積胄雜奉為贓，炎遣員寓蔓劾峭詆，貶汀州司馬。

translations.literal: It happened that men of Zhou's bureau accumulated miscellaneous gifts to Zhou as bribery; Yan sent Yuan Yu to impeach him with harsh slander, and he was demoted to Ting Prefecture Vice Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Men in Zhou's bureau had accumulated miscellaneous gifts to him as bribes. Yan sent Yuan Yu to impeach him harshly, and Zhou was demoted to vice administrator of Ting Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 稍遷京兆少尹，以父名不拜，換國子司業。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to Junior Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao; because of his father's name he did not accept the appointment and was changed to Vice Rector of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to junior metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, but because the title echoed his father's name he declined it and was reassigned as vice rector of the imperial university.

sentences.zh: 遷江西觀察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jiangxi Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to observation commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 初，李兼嘗罷南昌卒千餘人，收資稟為月進，胄白罷之。

translations.literal: Earlier Li Jian had once dismissed more than a thousand Nanchang soldiers and collected their pay allotments as monthly tribute; Zhou reported this and had it abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Jian had dismissed more than a thousand Nanchang soldiers and diverted their pay as monthly tribute to the court. Zhou reported the abuse and had it stopped.

sentences.zh: 樊澤徙襄州，宰相議所代，德宗雅記胄才，遂拜荊南節度使。

translations.literal: Fan Ze was transferred from Xiang Prefecture; the chief ministers discussed his replacement. Dezong had long noted Zhou's talent, and so appointed him Jingnan Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Ze left Xiang Prefecture, the chief ministers debated his replacement. Dezong had long noted Zhou's ability and appointed him military commissioner of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 是時，方鎮爭剝下希恩，制重錦異綾，名貢奉，有中使者，即悉公帑市歡。

translations.literal: At that time the regional commanders competed in stripping their subjects to seek favor, making heavy brocades and rare silks called tribute offerings; when there was a palace envoy, they would exhaust the public treasury to buy his goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commanders competed to squeeze their subjects and curry favor, weaving costly silks called tribute offerings. When a palace envoy arrived, they emptied the public treasury to win him over.

sentences.zh: 胄待之有節，獻餉直不數金，宴勞止三爵。

translations.literal: Zhou treated them with moderation; tribute gifts were worth only a few pieces of gold, and banquets to entertain them stopped at three rounds of wine.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou treated them with restraint: his gifts were worth only a few taels of gold, and his banquets stopped at three rounds of wine.

sentences.zh: 是時武臣多粗暴庸人，待賓介不以禮，少失意，則以罪中傷之，胄亦劾斥其管記，世恨胄之流於俗。

translations.literal: At that time military men were mostly crude and mediocre; they did not treat staff with courtesy, and if slightly displeased would slander them with crimes. Zhou also impeached and expelled their secretaries. The age resented Zhou as sliding into vulgarity.
translations.idiomatic: Most military men of the day were crude mediocrities who treated staff discourteously and framed them at the slightest offense. Zhou impeached their secretaries as well, and contemporaries resented him as becoming worldly.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十五，贈尚書右僕射，謚曰成。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-five, was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and given the posthumous title Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-five, was posthumously honored as right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, and given the posthumous title Cheng.

sentences.zh: 陽嶠，其先北平人，世徙洛陽，北齊尚書右僕射休之四世孫。

translations.literal: Yang Jiao—his ancestors were from Beiping and for generations moved to Luoyang—was the fourth-generation descendant of Northern Qi Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jiao was descended from Beiping families who had long settled in Luoyang, and was the fourth-generation descendant of Northern Qi right vice director Xiu.

sentences.zh: 舉八科皆中，調將陵尉，累遷詹事司直。

translations.literal: He passed all eight examination categories, was appointed Jiangling Sheriff, and was repeatedly promoted to Direct Clerk in the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He passed all eight civil-service categories, was appointed sheriff of Jiangling, and rose to direct clerk in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 長安中，左右御史中丞桓彥範、袁恕己爭取為御史。

translations.literal: In Chang'an, the Left and Right Attending Censor-in-Chief Huan Yanfan and Yuan Shuji competed to obtain him as a censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an, attending censors-in-chief Huan Yanfan and Yuan Shuji both competed to recruit him as a censor.

sentences.zh: 楊再思素與嶠善，知其意不樂彈抨事，為語彥範，彥範曰：「為官擇人，豈待情樂乎？

translations.literal: Yang Zaisi had long been on good terms with Jiao and knew he was unwilling to enjoy impeachment affairs; he spoke to Yanfan. Yanfan said: "In office one selects men—how can one wait for personal pleasure?
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaisi, who was close to Jiao, knew he disliked impeachment work and spoke to Yanfan. Yanfan said, "Officials choose the right men for office. Must one wait for personal inclination?

sentences.zh: 唯不樂者固與之，以伸難進、抑躁求也。」

translations.literal: It is precisely those who are unwilling that one firmly gives it to, in order to extend the hard-to-advance and restrain the rash in seeking office."
translations.idiomatic: One should give the post precisely to those who dislike it, to encourage the reluctant and restrain the overeager."

sentences.zh: 遂為右臺侍御史。

translations.literal: He was then made Attending Censor of the Right Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao was then made attending censor of the right bureau.

sentences.zh: 久乃遷國子司業。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Vice Rector of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was transferred to vice rector of the imperial university.

sentences.zh: 嶠資謹飭好學，喜誘勸後生、修講舍，人以為善職。

translations.literal: Jiao was by nature careful, disciplined, and fond of learning; he delighted in guiding and encouraging younger students and repairing lecture halls, and people regarded this as a good office.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao was careful, disciplined, and devoted to learning. He encouraged younger students and repaired lecture halls, and people regarded his tenure as exemplary.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，進尚書右丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, he was advanced to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Jiao was promoted to right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時議建都督府，擇最吏，故嶠為涇州都督。

translations.literal: At that time they discussed establishing a protector-general's office and chose the best official, so Jiao became Protector-General of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated establishing a protector-general's office, it chose the best available official, and Jiao became protector-general of Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 議罷，歷魏州刺史、荊州長史、本道按察使，率以清白聞。

translations.literal: When the plan was abandoned, he served through Prefect of Wei, Long History of Jing, and investigation commissioner of his circuit, and in each case was known for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When the plan was dropped, he served as prefect of Wei, long history of Jing, and investigation commissioner of his circuit, earning a reputation for integrity everywhere he went.

sentences.zh: 魏州人嫠耳闕下，請嶠為刺史，故再治魏。

translations.literal: People of Wei, widows among them, waited at the palace gate and requested Jiao as prefect, so he governed Wei a second time.
translations.idiomatic: Widows and other people of Wei waited at the palace gate to request Jiao as their prefect, and he governed Wei a second time.

sentences.zh: 入為國子祭酒，封北平縣伯。

translations.literal: He entered court as Rector of the Imperial University and was enfeoffed as Baron of Beiping County.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as rector of the imperial university and was enfeoffed as baron of Beiping County.

sentences.zh: 引尹知章、範行恭、趙玄默為學官，皆名儒冠雲。

translations.literal: He brought in Yin Zhizhang, Fan Xinggong, and Zhao Xuanmo as academic officers—all famed Confucians towering above the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Yin Zhizhang, Fan Xinggong, and Zhao Xuanmo as academic officers, all renowned scholars of the age.

sentences.zh: 生徒遊惰者至督以鞭楚，人怨之，乘夜毆嶠道中，事聞，詔捕毆者殺之。

translations.literal: Idle and lazy students he even supervised with the lash; people resented this, and one night they beat Jiao on the road. When the matter was reported, an edict ordered the assailants captured and executed.
translations.idiomatic: He even flogged idle students, provoking resentment. One night assailants beat him on the road. When the report reached court, the emperor ordered them captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 嶠撫孤侄與子均，常語人曰：「吾備位方伯，而心亦昔時一尉耳。」

translations.literal: Jiao treated his orphaned nephew and his son equally and often told people: "I hold a regional governor's post in name only, but in heart I am still the same sheriff I once was."
translations.idiomatic: Jiao treated his orphaned nephew and his son alike and often said, "I hold a regional governor's title, but in my heart I am still the same sheriff I once was."

sentences.zh: 以老致仕。

translations.literal: He retired on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: He retired on account of old age.

sentences.zh: 卒，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: He died and was given the posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 宋慶禮，洺州永年人。

translations.literal: Song Qingli was a native of Yongnian in Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qingli was a native of Yongnian in Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 擢明經，補衛尉。

translations.literal: He was selected through the Mingjing examination and appointed to the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination and entered the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 武後詔侍御史桓彥範行河北，鄣斷居庸、五回等路，以支突厥，召慶禮與議，見其方略，器之。

translations.literal: Empress Wu ordered Attending Censor Huan Yanfan to tour Hebei, block the roads at Juyong, Wuhui, and elsewhere to support against the Turks, and summoned Qingli to discuss it; seeing his strategy, she valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu ordered attending censor Huan Yanfan to tour Hebei and block routes such as Juyong and Wuhui against the Turks. Qingli was summoned to the discussions, and his strategic grasp won her esteem.

sentences.zh: 俄遷大理評事，為嶺南采訪使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Reviewing Official in the Court of Judicial Review and made Lingnan Investigation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to reviewing official in the Court of Judicial Review and made investigation commissioner of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 時崖、振五州首領更相掠，民苦於兵，使者至，輒苦瘴癘，莫敢往。

translations.literal: At that time the chieftains of the five prefectures Ya and Zhen raided one another in turn; the people suffered from warfare. When envoys arrived they always suffered miasma and pestilence, and none dared go.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftains of the five Ya and Zhen prefectures were raiding one another, and the people suffered from constant warfare. Envoys who arrived usually fell ill to miasma, and none dared go.

sentences.zh: 慶禮身到其境，諭首領大誼，皆釋仇相親，州土以安，罷戍卒五千。

translations.literal: Qingli went in person to that region, instructed the chieftains in great principle, and all released their enmities and became kin; the prefectures were thereby pacified and five thousand garrison troops were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Qingli went in person, instructed the chieftains in principle, and persuaded them to end their feuds. The region was pacified and five thousand garrison troops were withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 歷監察、殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He served through Investigating Censor and Palace Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as investigating censor and palace attending censor.

sentences.zh: 以習識邊事，拜河東、河北營田使。

translations.literal: Because he was versed in frontier affairs, he was appointed Garrison-Farming Commissioner for Hedong and Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Because he knew frontier affairs well, he was appointed garrison-farming commissioner for Hedong and Hebei.

sentences.zh: 善騎，日能馳數百里。

translations.literal: He was skilled at riding and could gallop several hundred li in a day.
translations.idiomatic: He was an expert rider and could cover several hundred li in a day.

sentences.zh: 性甘於勞苦，然好興作，濱塞掘阱植兵，以邀虜徑，議者蚩其不切事。

translations.literal: By nature he was willing to endure hardship, yet he loved construction projects, digging pits and planting troops along the border passes to ambush barbarian routes; critics scorned this as impractical.
translations.idiomatic: He was willing to endure hardship, yet loved building projects, digging pits and posting troops along the frontier to ambush enemy routes. Critics dismissed this as impractical.

sentences.zh: 稍遷貝州刺史，復為河北支度營田使。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to Prefect of Bei and again made Hebei Branch Garrison-Farming Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to prefect of Bei and again made branch garrison-farming commissioner of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 初，營州都督府治柳城，扼制奚、契丹。

translations.literal: Initially the Ying Prefecture Protector-General's government was at Liucheng, controlling the Xi and Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the protector-general of Ying Prefecture was based at Liucheng, controlling the Xi and Khitan.

sentences.zh: 武後時，趙文翙失兩蕃情，攻殘其府，更治東漁陽城。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time Zhao Wenhui lost the goodwill of the two tribes; they attacked and ravaged his headquarters, and the seat was moved to Eastern Yuyang City.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu, Zhao Wenhui lost the goodwill of both tribes. They attacked and destroyed his headquarters, and the seat was moved to Eastern Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 玄宗時，奚、契丹款附，帝欲復治故城，宋璟固爭不可，獨慶禮執處其利，乃詔與太子詹事姜師度、左驍衛將軍邵宏等為使，築裁三旬畢。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xuanzong's time the Xi and Khitan submitted in good faith; the Emperor wished to restore governance to the old city. Song Jing firmly argued it could not be done, but Qingli alone insisted on its advantage. An edict made him commissioner together with Heir Apparent Household Grand Mentor Jiang Shidu, Left Martial Guards General Shao Hong, and others; construction was completed in thirty days.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanzong the Xi and Khitan submitted peacefully, and the emperor wished to restore the old city. Song Jing strongly opposed the plan, but Qingli alone argued for its benefits. He was commissioned with Jiang Shidu and Shao Hong, and the city was rebuilt in thirty days.

sentences.zh: 俄兼營州都督，開屯田八十餘所，追拔漁陽、淄青沒戶還舊田宅，又集商胡立邸肆。

translations.literal: Soon he was concurrently Protector-General of Ying, opened more than eighty garrison-farms, recovered households lost to Yuyang and Ziqing and restored their old fields and homes, and also gathered merchant Hu to establish shops.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became concurrent protector-general of Ying, opened more than eighty garrison farms, recovered households lost in Yuyang and Ziqing and restored their lands, and gathered Sogdian merchants to establish markets.

sentences.zh: 不數年，倉廥充，居人蕃輯。

translations.literal: Within a few years the granaries were full and the inhabitants multiplied and gathered in prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the granaries were full and the population flourished.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as minister of works.

sentences.zh: 慶禮為政嚴，少私，吏畏威不敢犯。

translations.literal: Qingli's administration was strict and with little private interest; officials feared his authority and did not dare offend.
translations.idiomatic: Qingli governed strictly and without private interest. Officials feared his authority and dared not transgress.

sentences.zh: 太常博士張星以好巧自是，謚曰「專」。

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices Erudite Zhang Xing, relying on cleverness and self-satisfaction, gave the posthumous title "Zhuan" (Single-minded).
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Zhang Xing of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, relying on his own cleverness, proposed the posthumous title Zhuan, meaning single-minded.

sentences.zh: 禮部員外郎張九齡申駁曰：「慶禮國勞臣，在邊垂三十年。

translations.literal: Ministry of Rites Vice Director Zhang Jiuling submitted a rebuttal: "Qingli was a meritorious minister of the state who served on the frontier for thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: Vice director Zhang Jiuling of the Ministry of Rites objected: "Qingli was a meritorious servant of the state who spent thirty years on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 往城營州，士才數千，無甲兵強衛，指期而往，不失所慮，遂罷海運，收歲儲，邊亭晏然。

translations.literal: When he went to build the city at Ying, he had only a few thousand laborers and no strong armor or guards, yet he arrived within the set term without failing his plans, then abolished sea transport, gathered annual stores, and the frontier posts were tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: When he rebuilt Ying, he had only a few thousand laborers and no strong guard force, yet he finished on schedule as planned, ended sea transport, filled the annual stores, and brought the frontier to peace.

sentences.zh: 其功可推，不當醜謚。」

translations.literal: His merit can be extended and praised; he should not receive an ugly posthumous title."
translations.idiomatic: His achievements deserve praise, not a disparaging posthumous title."

sentences.zh: 慶禮兄子辭玉亦自詣闕訴。

translations.literal: Qingli's elder brother's son Ciyu also went in person to the palace gate to appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Qingli's nephew Ciyu also went to court in person to appeal.

sentences.zh: 改謚曰敬。

translations.literal: The posthumous title was changed to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The posthumous title was changed to Jing.

sentences.zh: 楊玚，字瑤光，華州華陰人。

translations.literal: Yang Chang, style name Yaoguang, was a native of Huayin in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chang, styled Yaoguang, was a native of Huayin in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五世祖縉，為陳中書舍人，名屬文，終交、愛九州都督、武康郡公。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Jin was a Chen Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat, famed for literary composition, and ended as Protector-General of the Nine Prefectures of Jiao and Ai and Duke of Wukang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Jin had been a Chen drafting attendant famed for literature and ended as protector-general of Jiao and Ai and duke of Wukang.

sentences.zh: 子林甫代領都督，隋滅陳，逾三年乃降，徙長安。

translations.literal: His son Linpu succeeded as protector-general. When Sui destroyed Chen, only after more than three years did he surrender, and he was moved to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: His son Linpu succeeded as protector-general. After Sui destroyed Chen, he surrendered only after more than three years and was resettled in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 林甫字衛卿，為柳城太守，高祖軍興，遣其子琮招之，挈郡以來，授檢校總管，足疾不能造朝。

translations.literal: Linpu, style name Weiqing, was Administrator of Liucheng. When Gaozu raised his army, he sent his son Cong to summon him; he brought his commandery and came, was appointed Acting Protector-General, but had foot ailment and could not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Linpu, styled Weiqing, was administrator of Liucheng. When Gaozu raised his army, he sent his son Cong to summon him. Linpu brought his commandery over and was appointed acting protector-general, but foot ailment kept him from court.

sentences.zh: 帝以絳州寒涼，拜刺史，累封宜春郡公。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Jiang Prefecture was cold and cool, appointed him prefect and repeatedly enfeoffed him as Duke of Yichun Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jiang Prefecture was cool, the emperor appointed him prefect there and repeatedly enfeoffed him as duke of Yichun.

sentences.zh: 琮字孝璋，為上津令。

translations.literal: Cong, style name Xiaozhang, was Magistrate of Shangjin.
translations.idiomatic: Cong, styled Xiaozhang, was magistrate of Shangjin.

sentences.zh: 會天下亂，去官，與秦王同裏居。

translations.literal: When the realm fell into disorder he left office and lived in the same neighborhood as the Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm fell into chaos he left office and lived in the same neighborhood as the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 武德初，為王府參軍，兼庫直。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude he was an aide in the prince's establishment and concurrently a vault attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude reign he served as an aide in the prince's establishment and as vault attendant.

sentences.zh: 隱太子事平，詔親王、宰相一人入宴，而琮獨預，太宗賜《懷昔賦》，申以恩意。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Crown Prince affair was settled, an edict allowed one imperial prince and one chief minister to enter the banquet, but Cong alone was included. Taizong bestowed the Rhapsody on Recalling the Past and expressed his favor in affection.
translations.idiomatic: After the Hidden Crown Prince affair was settled, the edict allowed one imperial prince and one chief minister into the banquet, but Cong alone was included. Taizong gave him the Rhapsody on Recalling the Past and expressed his personal affection.

sentences.zh: 歷沔、綏二州刺史。

translations.literal: He served through the two prefectures Mian and Sui as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Mian and Sui.

sentences.zh: 姆饋孺子以餅，妻偽受而棄之垣外，人咨其廉。

translations.literal: A nurse presented cakes to the children; his wife pretended to accept them and threw them outside the wall. People praised his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When a nurse brought cakes for the children, his wife pretended to accept them and threw them outside the wall. People praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 玚始為麟遊令，時竇懷貞大營金仙、玉直二觀，檄取畿內嘗負逆人貲者，暴斂之以佐費，玚拒不應。

translations.literal: Chang first served as Magistrate of Linyou. At that time Dou Huaizhen was greatly building the Jinxian and Yuzhi monasteries, issuing orders to take within the capital region those who had once owed money to rebels and extorting them violently to assist the costs; Chang refused to comply.
translations.idiomatic: Chang first served as magistrate of Linyou. Dou Huaizhen was building the Jinxian and Yuzhi monasteries on a grand scale and ordered the capital region to seize funds from anyone who had once owed money to rebels. Chang refused.

sentences.zh: 懷貞怒曰：「縣令而拒大夫命乎？」

translations.literal: Huaizhen said angrily: "A magistrate refusing a grand master's order?"
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen raged, "A county magistrate defying a grand master's order?"

sentences.zh: 玚曰：「所論者民冤抑也，位高下乎何取？」

translations.literal: Chang said: "What is at issue is the people's grievance and oppression—what does rank high or low have to do with it?"
translations.idiomatic: Chang replied, "What matters is the people's grievance. What does rank have to do with it?"

sentences.zh: 懷貞壯其對，為止。

translations.literal: Huaizhen admired his reply and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen was impressed and desisted.

sentences.zh: 初，韋後表民二十二為丁限，及敗，有司追趣其課，玚執不可，曰：「韋氏當國，擅擢士大夫，赦罪人，皆不改，奚獨取已寬之人重斂其租？

translations.literal: Earlier Empress Wei had memorialized to make twenty-two the adult male quota; when she fell, the offices pursued collection of the tax. Chang held that this could not be done and said: "When the Wei clan held the state they arbitrarily promoted scholars and officials and pardoned criminals—all unchanged—why alone take those already given leniency and heavily levy their rents again?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Empress Wei had lowered the adult-male quota to twenty-two. After her fall the offices tried to collect the difference. Chang objected: "When the Wei clan ruled, they promoted favorites and pardoned criminals without reversal. Why now squeeze those already given relief and tax them again?

sentences.zh: 非所以保下之宜。」

translations.literal: This is not the proper way to protect those below."
translations.idiomatic: That is no way to protect the people."

sentences.zh: 遂止不課，由是名顯當世。

translations.literal: Thereupon collection was stopped, and from this his name became prominent in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Collection was halted, and his reputation spread through the age.

sentences.zh: 擢累侍御史。

translations.literal: He was selected and repeatedly promoted to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attending censor.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹崔日知貪沓不法，玚與大夫李傑謀劾舉之，反為日知先構。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao Cui Rizhi was greedy, grasping, and lawless. Chang and Censor-in-Chief Li Jie plotted to impeach him, but Rizhi framed them first.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan governor Cui Rizhi of Jingzhao was greedy and lawless. Chang and censor-in-chief Li Jie planned to impeach him, but Rizhi framed them first.

sentences.zh: 玚廷奏曰：「肅繩之司，一為恐脅所屈，開奸人謀，則御史府可廢。」

translations.literal: Chang memorialized at court: "The office that maintains discipline—if once bent by intimidation, opening the way for crafty men's schemes—then the Censorate can be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Chang memorialized at court: "If the office that upholds discipline can be cowed by intimidation and open the way for schemers, the Censorate might as well be abolished."

sentences.zh: 玄宗直之，令傑還視事，而逐日知。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong upheld him, ordered Jie to return to his duties, and expelled Rizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong upheld him, restored Jie to office, and expelled Rizhi.

sentences.zh: 玚進歷御史中丞、戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Chang advanced through Vice Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Chang rose to vice censor-in-chief and vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗召宰相大臣議天下戶版延英殿，玚言利病尤詳，帝咨賞。

translations.literal: The Emperor once summoned chief ministers and great officials to discuss the realm's household registers in the Hall of Englightened Administration; Chang spoke on benefits and harms with especial detail, and the Emperor commended and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once summoned chief ministers to discuss the realm's household registers in the Hall of Enlightened Administration. Chang analyzed the benefits and harms in exceptional detail, and the emperor praised him.

sentences.zh: 於是宇文融建檢脫戶餘口，玚執不便。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yuwen Rong proposed inspecting and registering surplus household members; Chang held that this was inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Rong then proposed a survey to register surplus household members. Chang objected that it was unwise.

sentences.zh: 融方貴，公卿唵默唯唯，獨玚抗議，故出為華州刺史。

translations.literal: Rong was then in favor; the dukes and ministers were silent and assented—only Chang protested, and therefore he was sent out as Prefect of Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was then in favor, and the high officials kept silent. Only Chang protested, so he was sent out as prefect of Hua.

sentences.zh: 帝封太山，集樂工山下，居喪者亦在行。

translations.literal: When the Emperor performed the feng sacrifice on Mount Tai, he gathered musicians below the mountain, and those in mourning were also in the procession.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor performed the feng sacrifice on Mount Tai, he gathered musicians at the foot of the mountain, and men in mourning were also in the procession.

sentences.zh: 玚謂起苴绖使和鐘律，非人情所堪，帝許，乃免。

translations.literal: Chang said that making them remove mourning hemp and harmonize bells and pitch was beyond what human feeling could bear; the Emperor consented, and they were exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said that forcing mourners to remove their hemp garments and tune the ritual music was more than human feeling could bear. The emperor agreed and exempted them.

sentences.zh: 入為國子祭酒，表大儒王迥質、尹子路、白履忠等三人教授國子。

translations.literal: He entered court as Rector of the Imperial University and memorialized that the great Confucians Wang Huizhi, Yin Zilu, and Bai Lvzhong, three men, should instruct at the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as rector of the imperial university and recommended the great scholars Wang Huizhi, Yin Zilu, and Bai Lvzhong to teach there.

sentences.zh: 有詔迥質諫議大夫、皇太子侍讀；

translations.literal: An edict made Huizhi Remonstrance Grand Master and Reader to the Heir Apparent;
translations.idiomatic: Huizhi was made remonstrance grand master and reader to the heir apparent;

sentences.zh: 履忠老不任職，拜朝散大夫罷歸；

translations.literal: Lvzhong was old and unable to take office, so he was made Grand Master of Palace Leisure and sent home;
translations.idiomatic: Lvzhong was too old to serve and was made grand master of palace leisure before returning home;

sentences.zh: 子路直弘文館。

translations.literal: Zilu was assigned directly to the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Zilu was assigned to the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 皆有名。

translations.literal: All had reputation.
translations.idiomatic: All were well known.

sentences.zh: 玚奏：「有司帖試明經，不質大義，乃取年頭、月尾、孤經、絕句，且今習《春秋》三家、《儀禮》者才十二，恐諸家廢無日，請帖平文以存學家，其能通者稍加優宦，獎孤學。」

translations.literal: Chang memorialized: "The offices in posting examinations for Mingjing do not test great principle, but take year-head, month-tail, isolated passages, and cut-off lines. Moreover those now studying the three schools of the Spring and Autumn Annals and the Book of Rites are only twelve—I fear the various schools will be abandoned without delay. I request posting plain texts to preserve the scholarly families; those who can master them should receive slightly better offices, rewarding solitary learning."
translations.idiomatic: Chang memorialized: "In the Mingjing examinations the offices test trivial passages rather than great principle, and only twelve candidates now study the three Spring and Autumn traditions and the Book of Rites. I fear those schools will soon die out. I ask that plain texts be posted to preserve scholarly lineages, with better appointments for those who truly master them, to reward dedicated learning."

sentences.zh: 從之，因詔以三家《傳》、《儀禮》出身者不任散官，遂著令。

translations.literal: This was followed, and an edict was issued that those who entered office through the three commentaries and the Book of Rites should not hold scattered offices; this was then written into regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted. Graduates in the three commentaries and the Book of Rites were barred from scattered offices, and the rule was codified.

sentences.zh: 生徒為玚立頌太學門。

translations.literal: The students erected a eulogy for Chang at the gate of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: The students erected an inscription in his praise at the gate of the imperial university.

sentences.zh: 又言：「古者卿大夫子弟及諸侯歲貢小學之異者入太學，漸漬禮樂，知朝廷君臣之序，班以品類，分以師長，三德四教，學成然後爵之。

translations.literal: He also said: "In antiquity the sons and younger brothers of ministers and grandees and the yearly tribute of outstanding pupils from the elementary schools entered the Imperial University, were steeped in ritual and music, knew the order of ruler and minister at court, were classed by category, divided among teachers, received the three virtues and four teachings, and only after completing their studies were ennobled.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "In antiquity the sons of nobles and the outstanding pupils presented yearly by the marquisates entered the imperial university, were steeped in ritual and music, learned the order of court, were grouped by rank and assigned teachers, received the three virtues and four teachings, and were ennobled only after completing their studies.

sentences.zh: 唐興，二監舉者千百數，當選者十之二，考功覆校以第，謂經明行修，故無多少之限。

translations.literal: When Tang arose, the two directorates presented candidates by the hundreds and thousands; those selected were two in ten. The Ministry of Personnel reviewed and ranked them by grade, calling it clarity in the classics and cultivation in conduct, and therefore there was no limit on number.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang, the two directorates presented hundreds or thousands of candidates, of whom about two in ten were chosen. The Ministry of Personnel reviewed and ranked them as men of classical learning and cultivated conduct, without a fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 今考功限天下明經、進士歲百人，二監之得無幾，然則學徒費官稟，而博士濫天祿者也。

translations.literal: Now the Ministry of Personnel limits Mingjing and Jinshi throughout the realm to one hundred per year; the two directorates gain almost nothing. Thus students waste official stipends while erudites abuse Heaven's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Ministry of Personnel limits Mingjing and jinshi graduates empire-wide to one hundred a year, leaving the directorates almost nothing. Students waste state stipends while erudites draw salaries they do not earn.

sentences.zh: 且以流外及諸色仕者歲二千，過明經、進士十倍，胥史浮虛之徒，毛先王禮義，非得與服勤道業者挈長短、絕輕重也。

translations.literal: Moreover those entering office from outside the regular stream and various categories number two thousand yearly—ten times more than Mingjing and Jinshi. Clerks and floating empty men slight the ritual righteousness of the former kings; they truly cannot be set against those who diligently serve the Way in weighing light and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover two thousand men enter office each year through irregular channels, ten times the number of Mingjing and jinshi graduates. Petty clerks and hollow careerists care nothing for the ritual teachings of the former kings and cannot be weighed against men who earnestly pursue the Way.

sentences.zh: 國家啟庠序，廣化導，將有以用而勸進之。

translations.literal: The state opens schools and broadens transformation and guidance, intending to employ men thereby and encourage advancement.
translations.idiomatic: The state opens schools and broadens moral instruction in order to employ worthy men and encourage advancement.

sentences.zh: 有司為限約以黜退之，欲望俊乂在朝，難矣。」

translations.literal: Yet the offices set limits to reject and dismiss them—to desire outstanding talent at court is difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the offices set quotas that shut men out. To hope for outstanding talent at court becomes difficult."

sentences.zh: 帝然其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his argument.

sentences.zh: 再遷大理卿，以疾辭，改左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Minister of Justice, declined on account of illness, and was changed to Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made minister of justice, declined on account of illness, and was reassigned as left regular attendant of the cavalry.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十八，贈戶部尚書，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-eight, was posthumously made Minister of Revenue, and given the posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-eight, was posthumously honored as minister of revenue, and given the posthumous title Zhen.

sentences.zh: 玚常嘆士大夫不能用古禮，因其家冠、婚、喪、祭，乃據舊典為之節文，揖讓威儀，哭踴衰殺，無有違者。

translations.literal: Chang often lamented that scholar-officials could not use ancient ritual. For his family's capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice rites he therefore followed the old canons in their regulations, bowing and yielding with dignified ceremony, wailing and leaping with graded mourning—none deviated.
translations.idiomatic: Chang often lamented that scholar-officials no longer observed ancient ritual. For his family's capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice ceremonies he followed the old canons in full, with proper bowing, yielding, wailing, and graded mourning, and no one deviated.

sentences.zh: 在官清白，吏請立石紀德，玚曰：「事益於人，書名史氏足矣。

translations.literal: In office he was pure and clean. Clerks asked to erect a stone recording his virtue. Chang said: "If affairs benefit the people, having one's name written in the historical records is enough.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was incorruptible. When clerks asked to erect a stone praising his virtue, Chang said, "If one's deeds benefit the people, having one's name in the historical records is enough.

sentences.zh: 若碑頌者，徒遣後人作碇石耳。」

translations.literal: As for steles and eulogies, they only make later people use them as mooring stones."
translations.idiomatic: Stele inscriptions only give later men something to tie their boats to."
