sentences.zh: 玚伯父誌操，頗剛簡，未遇時，著《閑居賦》自托，常曰：「得田十頃、僮婢十人，下有兄弟布粟之資，上可供先公伏臘足矣。」

translations.literal: Chang's father's elder brother Zhicao was rather stern and plain. Before he met his time he wrote the Rhapsody on Secluded Living to express himself and often said: "To obtain ten qing of fields and ten servants, with brothers below having cloth and grain for support and above being able to supply the ancestral offerings at the solstices is enough."
translations.idiomatic: Chang's uncle Zhicao was stern and plain. Before he found his place in the world he wrote the Rhapsody on Secluded Living and often said, "Ten qing of land, ten servants, enough grain for my brothers below and enough offerings for my ancestors above—that is all I need."

sentences.zh: 位終司屬卿、安平縣男。

translations.literal: He ended as Director of the Imperial Clan and Baron of Anping County.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as director of the imperial clan and baron of Anping County.

sentences.zh: 玚從父兄晏，精《孝經》學，常手寫數十篇，可教者輒遺之。

translations.literal: Chang's elder cousin by a collateral line Yan was expert in the Classic of Filial Piety, often copied several tens of chapters by hand, and whenever he found someone teachable would give them away.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's cousin Yan was expert in the Classic of Filial Piety, often copied dozens of chapters by hand, and gave them to anyone worth teaching.

sentences.zh: 崔隱甫，貝州武城人。

translations.literal: Cui Yinpu was a native of Wucheng in Bei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yinpu was a native of Wucheng in Bei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隋散騎侍郎儦曾孫。

translations.literal: He was the great-grandson of Sui Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Biao.
translations.idiomatic: He was the great-grandson of the Sui regular attendant of the cavalry Biao.

sentences.zh: 解褐左玉鈐衛兵曹參軍，遷殿侍御史內供奉。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the purple he was Left Jade Bell Guard Bureau Aide, then transferred to Palace Attending Censor in inner attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering office he was aide in the Left Jade Bell Guard Bureau, then became palace attending censor in inner attendance.

sentences.zh: 浮屠惠範倚太平公主脅人子女，隱甫劾狀，反為所擠，貶邛州司馬。

translations.literal: The Buddhist Huifan relied on Princess Taiping to coerce people's sons and daughters. Yinpu impeached him in detail but was in turn squeezed out and demoted to Qiong Prefecture Vice Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Huifan, backed by Princess Taiping, coerced people's sons and daughters. Yinpu impeached him but was squeezed out and demoted to vice administrator of Qiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 玄宗立，擢汾州長史，兼河東道支度營田使，遷洛陽令。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne he was promoted to Long History of Fen, concurrently Hedong Branch Supply and Garrison-Farming Commissioner, and transferred to Magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong took the throne, Yinpu was promoted to long history of Fen, made concurrent Hedong supply and garrison-farming commissioner, and transferred to magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 梨園弟子胡雛善笛，有寵，嘗負罪匿禁中。

translations.literal: Pear Garden disciple Hu Chu was skilled at the flute and in favor; he once committed a crime and hid in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Pear Garden performer Hu Chu was skilled at the flute and in imperial favor. Once guilty of a crime, he hid inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 帝以他事召隱甫，從容指曰：「就卿丐此人。」

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Yinpu on another matter and casually pointed, saying: "Through you I beg this man."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Yinpu on another matter and casually said, "I want you to hand this man over to me."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下輕臣而重樂工，請解官。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Your Majesty values a musician above your servant—I request to resign office."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Your Majesty values a musician above your servant. I ask to resign."

sentences.zh: 再拜出，帝遽謝，與胡雛，隱甫殺之，有詔貰死，不及矣。

translations.literal: He bowed twice and left. The Emperor hastily apologized and gave him Hu Chu; Yinpu executed him. An edict pardoned him from death, but it did not arrive in time.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed twice and left. The emperor hastily apologized and handed over Hu Chu. Yinpu executed him before a pardon could arrive.

sentences.zh: 賜隱甫百縑。

translations.literal: Yinpu was granted one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted Yinpu one hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 孫佺敗績於奚，擢隱甫并州司馬護邊，會兄逸甫疾甚，未及行，詔責逗留，下除河南令。

translations.literal: When Sun Zhan was defeated by the Xi, Yinpu was promoted to Bing Prefecture Vice Administrator to guard the border. It happened that his elder brother Yifu was gravely ill and he had not yet departed; an edict reproached him for delay and demoted him to Magistrate of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Zhan's defeat by the Xi, Yinpu was promoted to vice administrator of Bing to guard the frontier. His brother Yifu fell gravely ill before he could depart. The court rebuked him for delay and demoted him to magistrate of Henan.

sentences.zh: 累拜華州刺史、太原尹，入為河南尹。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed Prefect of Hua and Metropolitan Governor of Taiyuan, and entered court as Metropolitan Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to prefect of Hua and metropolitan governor of Taiyuan, then entered court as metropolitan governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 居三歲，進拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: After three years he was advanced to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he was promoted to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 初，臺無獄，凡有囚則系大理。

translations.literal: Initially the Censorate had no prison; whenever there were prisoners they were detained at the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the Censorate had no prison; prisoners were held at the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 貞觀時，李乾祐為大夫，始置獄，由是中丞、侍御史皆得系人。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era, when Li Qianyou was chief censor, a prison was first established, and from this the vice censors and attending censors could all detain people.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era chief censor Li Qianyou first established a Censorate prison, allowing vice censors and attending censors to detain suspects.

sentences.zh: 隱甫執故事，廢掘諸獄。

translations.literal: Yinpu held to precedent and abolished and filled in the prisons.
translations.idiomatic: Yinpu held to precedent and abolished the prisons.

sentences.zh: 其後患囚往來或漏泄，復系之廚院雲。

translations.literal: Later, fearing that prisoners coming and going might leak information, he again detained them in the kitchen courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Later, fearing leaks when prisoners were moved about, he detained them again in the kitchen courtyard.

sentences.zh: 臺中自監察御史而下，舊皆得顓事，無所承諮。

translations.literal: Within the bureau, from investigating censors downward, formerly all could handle matters exclusively without reporting for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, from investigating censors downward, everyone in the bureau could act on his own authority without reporting upward.

sentences.zh: 隱甫始一切令歸稟乃得行，有忤意輒劾正，多貶絀者，臺吏側目，威名赫然。

translations.literal: Yinpu first ordered that everything must be reported and approved before it could proceed; whoever displeased him was immediately impeached and corrected, and many were demoted or reduced—bureau clerks looked askance, and his awe-inspiring name blazed.
translations.idiomatic: Yinpu required every action to be reported and approved first. Anyone who crossed him was impeached, and many were demoted. The bureau clerks watched him in fear, and his reputation for severity blazed.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗詔校外官歲考。

translations.literal: The Emperor once ordered the annual evaluation of external officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once ordered the annual evaluation of external officials.

sentences.zh: 異時必委曲參審，竟春未定。

translations.literal: In other times they would certainly examine in exhaustive detail, and by the end of spring nothing was settled.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier times the reviews dragged on in exhaustive detail until spring ended without a decision.

sentences.zh: 隱甫一日會朝集使，詢逮檢實，其暮皆訖，議者服其敏。

translations.literal: Yinpu in one day convened the assembly envoys, inquired, pursued, inspected, and verified; by evening all was finished, and critics admired his swiftness.
translations.idiomatic: Yinpu convened the assembly envoys in a single day, questioned them, verified the records, and finished by evening. Observers marveled at his speed.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗謂曰：「卿為大夫，天下以為稱職。」

translations.literal: The Emperor once said to him: "As chief censor, the realm regards you as fulfilling the office."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told him, "As censor-in-chief, the realm regards you as fully equal to the post."

sentences.zh: 張說當國，隱甫素惡之，乃與中丞宇文融、李林甫暴其過，不宜處位，說賜罷；

translations.literal: Zhang Yue held the state; Yinpu had long hated him. He therefore joined Vice Censors Yuwen Rong and Li Linfu in exposing his faults, saying he was unfit to hold position, and Yue was bestowed dismissal;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yue dominated the government, Yinpu, who had long despised him, joined vice censors Yuwen Rong and Li Linfu in exposing his faults and arguing that he was unfit for office. Yue was dismissed;

sentences.zh: 然帝嫉朋黨，免其官，使侍母。

translations.literal: yet the Emperor detested factional cliques, removed him from office, and had him attend his mother.
translations.idiomatic: but the emperor detested factional cliques, removed Yinpu from office, and had him attend his mother.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，復為大夫。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was again made chief censor.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was restored as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部尚書，兼河南尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Justice and concurrently Metropolitan Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of justice and concurrent metropolitan governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 帝還京師，即拜東都留守。

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned to the capital he was immediately appointed Protector of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, Yinpu was immediately appointed protector of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 累封清河郡公。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as duke of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈益州大都督，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Protector-General of Yi and given the posthumous title Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as protector-general of Yi, with the posthumous title Zhong.

sentences.zh: 始，帝欲相隱甫也，謂曰：「牛仙客可與語，卿常見否？」

translations.literal: At first the Emperor wished to make Yinpu chief minister and said to him: "Niu Xianke is someone one can talk with—do you often see him?"
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor wished to make Yinpu chief minister and asked, "Niu Xianke is worth talking with. Do you see him often?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「未也。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Not yet."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Not yet."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「可見之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "You may see him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You should meet him."

sentences.zh: 隱甫終不詣。

translations.literal: Yinpu in the end never went.
translations.idiomatic: Yinpu never went.

sentences.zh: 他日又問，對如初。

translations.literal: Another day he asked again, and the answer was as before.
translations.idiomatic: When asked again later, he gave the same answer.

sentences.zh: 帝乃不用。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon did not use him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then did not appoint him.

sentences.zh: 子弟或問故，答曰：「吾不以其人微易之也，其材不逮中人，可與之對耶？」

translations.literal: His sons and younger relatives sometimes asked the reason. He answered: "I do not treat him lightly because his person is humble; his talent does not reach the middling man—how could one converse with him as an equal?"
translations.idiomatic: When relatives asked why, he said, "I do not look down on him because he is humble. His talent does not even reach the middling level. How could I treat him as an equal?"

sentences.zh: 隱甫所至絜介自守，明吏治，在職以強正稱雲。

translations.literal: Wherever Yinpu went he was pure and guarded himself, clear in official governance, and in office was famed for forceful uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Yinpu served he remained scrupulously self-restrained, skilled in administration, and famed for uncompromising uprightness.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：嚴挺之拒宰相不肯見李林甫，崔隱甫違詔不屈牛仙客，信剛者乎！

translations.literal: The encomium says: Yan Tingzhi refused the chief minister and would not see Li Linfu; Cui Yinpu defied an edict and would not yield to Niu Xianke—truly men of firmness!
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Yan Tingzhi refused to see chief minister Li Linfu; Cui Yinpu defied an edict rather than yield to Niu Xianke. Truly they were men of iron resolve!

sentences.zh: 二人坐是皆不得相，彼亦各申其誌也。

translations.literal: Both men for this reason were unable to become chief ministers, yet each also expressed his own resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Both men were kept from the chief ministership for this, yet each thereby expressed his own resolve.

sentences.zh: 管夷吾以編棧諭之，信曲與直不相函哉！

translations.literal: Guan Zhong used plaited rafts as a metaphor—truly bent and straight cannot be contained in one case!
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong used plaited rafts as a metaphor: truly the bent and the straight cannot be bundled together!

sentences.zh: 李尚隱，其先出趙郡，徙貫萬年。

translations.literal: Li Shangyin—his ancestors came from Zhao Commandery and moved to register in Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shangyin's ancestors came from Zhao Commandery and later registered in Wannian.

sentences.zh: 年二十，舉明經，再調下邽主簿，州刺史姚珽說其能，器之。

translations.literal: At age twenty he passed the Mingjing examination, was twice transferred as Xiayi Registrar, and Prefect Yao Ting of the province spoke of his ability and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he passed the Mingjing examination and served twice as registrar of Xiayi. Prefect Yao Ting praised his ability and valued him.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，左臺中丞侯令德為關內黜陟使，尚隱佐之，以最擢左臺監察御史。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong era, Left Bureau Vice Censor Hou Lingde was Guannei Promotion and Demotion Commissioner; Shangyin assisted him and, rated highest, was promoted to Left Bureau Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong reign, vice censor Hou Lingde of the left bureau was Guannei promotion and demotion commissioner. Shangyin assisted him, ranked highest, and was promoted to investigating censor of the left bureau.

sentences.zh: 於是，崔湜、鄭愔典吏部選，附勢幸，銓擬不平，至逆用三年員闕，材廉者軋不進，俄而相踵知政事，尚隱與御史李懷讓顯劾其罪，湜等皆斥去。

translations.literal: Thereupon Cui Shi and Zheng Yin controlled personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel, attached themselves to the powerful and favored, made unfair nominations, even inverting use of three years' quota vacancies; men of talent and integrity were squeezed out and could not advance. Soon they succeeded one another in knowing state affairs. Shangyin with Censor Li Huairang openly impeached their crimes, and Shi and the others were all expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Shi and Zheng Yin then ran Ministry of Personnel selection, curried favor with the powerful, made unfair appointments, and even misused three years of vacant posts so worthy men could not advance. When they rose in turn to chief minister, Shangyin and censor Li Huairang openly impeached them, and they were all expelled.

sentences.zh: 睦州刺史馮昭泰性鷙刻，人憚其強，嘗誣系桐廬令李師旦二百餘家為妖蠱，有詔御史覆驗，皆稱病不肯往。

translations.literal: Muzhou Prefect Feng Zhaotai was fierce and harsh by nature; people feared his strength. He once falsely imprisoned more than two hundred households of Tonglu Magistrate Li Shidan as practitioners of sorcery and witchcraft. An edict ordered censors to re-investigate, but all claimed illness and refused to go.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhou prefect Feng Zhaotai was fierce and harsh, and people feared him. He once falsely imprisoned more than two hundred households of Tonglu magistrate Li Shidan on charges of sorcery. Censors were ordered to reinvestigate, but all claimed illness and refused to go.

sentences.zh: 尚隱曰：「善良方蒙枉，不為申明，可乎？」

translations.literal: Shangyin said: "Good and innocent people are now suffering wrong—can we fail to clarify this for them?"
translations.idiomatic: Shangyin said, "Innocent people are being wronged. Can we fail to clear them?"

sentences.zh: 因請行，果推雪其冤。

translations.literal: He therefore requested to go and in the end overturned and cleared their injustice.
translations.idiomatic: He volunteered to go and in the end cleared their names.

sentences.zh: 湜、愔復當路，乃出尚隱為伊闕令，懷讓魏令。

translations.literal: When Shi and Yin again held the road of power, they sent Shangyin out as Magistrate of Yique and Huairang as Magistrate of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi and Yin returned to power, they sent Shangyin out as magistrate of Yique and Huairang as magistrate of Wei.

sentences.zh: 湜等伏誅，玄宗知尚隱方嚴，由定州司馬擢吏部員外郎，懷讓自河陽令拜兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Shi and the others were executed, Xuanzong knew Shangyin was upright and strict; from Ding Prefecture Vice Administrator he was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel, and Huairang from Magistrate of Heyang was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi and his allies were executed, Xuanzong knew Shangyin to be upright and promoted him from vice administrator of Ding to vice director in the Ministry of Personnel. Huairang rose from magistrate of Heyang to vice director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 懷讓，蓚人，後歷給事中。

translations.literal: Huairang was a man of Shuo and later served through Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Huairang was from Shuo and later served as drafting attendant.

sentences.zh: 尚隱以將作少監營橋陵，封高邑縣男。

translations.literal: Shangyin, as Vice Director of the Directorate for Palace Buildings, constructed Qiao Mausoleum and was enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoyi County.
translations.idiomatic: As vice director of the Directorate for Palace Buildings, Shangyin constructed Qiao Mausoleum and was enfeoffed as baron of Gaoyi County.

sentences.zh: 未幾，進御史中丞。

translations.literal: Before long he was advanced to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 御史王旭招權，稍不制，仇家告其罪，尚隱窮治，具得奸贓，無假借，遂抵罪。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Xu gathered power and was gradually uncontrolled. An enemy household reported his crimes; Shangyin exhaustively investigated, fully obtained bribery and corruption, showed no indulgence, and he was brought to punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Xu gathered power and grew uncontrolled. Enemies reported his crimes. Shangyin investigated thoroughly, proved bribery and corruption without leniency, and brought him to justice.

sentences.zh: 進兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 俄出為蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as Prefect of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as prefect of Pu.

sentences.zh: 浮屠懷照者，自言母夢日入懷生己，鏤石著驗，聞人馮待徵等助實其言。

translations.literal: The Buddhist Huaizhao claimed that his mother dreamed the sun entered her bosom and gave birth to him; he carved stone to record verification, and men of reputation such as Feng Daizheng helped substantiate his words.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Huaizhao claimed his mother dreamed the sun entered her womb when she bore him. He carved stone inscriptions as proof, and men such as Feng Daizheng helped substantiate the claim.

sentences.zh: 尚隱劾處妖妄，詔流懷照播州。

translations.literal: Shangyin impeached and punished this demonic delusion; an edict exiled Huaizhao to Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyin impeached this as demonic fraud, and an edict exiled Huaizhao to Bo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 再遷河南尹。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Metropolitan Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to metropolitan governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 尚隱性剛亮，論議皆披心示誠，處事分明，禦下不苛密。

translations.literal: Shangyin was by nature firm and bright; in discussion he always laid open his heart and showed sincerity, handled affairs clearly, and governed subordinates without harsh exactness.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyin was firm and candid by nature, spoke with open sincerity, judged affairs clearly, and governed subordinates without harsh exactness.

sentences.zh: 尤詳練故實，前後制令，誦記略無遺。

translations.literal: He was especially well versed in old precedents; regulations and orders past and present he could recite from memory with scarcely anything omitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially versed in precedent and could recite regulations past and present from memory with little omission.

sentences.zh: 妖賊劉定高夜犯通洛門，尚隱坐不素覺，左遷桂州都督。

translations.literal: The demonic bandit Liu Dinggao by night attacked Tongluo Gate; Shangyin was punished for not having been aware beforehand and was demoted to Protector-General of Gui.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Liu Dinggao attacked Tongluo Gate by night. Shangyin was punished for not detecting the threat in advance and demoted to protector-general of Gui.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使勞曰：「知卿忠公，然國法須爾。」

translations.literal: The Emperor sent an envoy to console him, saying: "I know you are loyal and public-spirited, yet the laws of the state require this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an envoy to console him, saying, "I know you are loyal and dutiful, yet state law requires this."

sentences.zh: 因賜雜彩百匹遣之。

translations.literal: He therefore granted one hundred bolts of variegated silks and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: He then granted him one hundred bolts of variegated silk and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 遷廣州都督、五府經略使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Protector-General of Guangzhou and Commissioner for Pacification of the Five Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to protector-general of Guangzhou and commissioner for pacification of the five prefectures.

sentences.zh: 及還，人或袖金以贈，尚隱曰：「吾自性分不可易，非畏人知也。」

translations.literal: When he returned, some tucked gold in their sleeves to present to him. Shangyin said: "By my nature I cannot be changed—this is not from fear that others would know."
translations.idiomatic: On his return, some tried to slip gold into his sleeve. Shangyin said, "My nature cannot be changed. This is not because I fear being found out."

sentences.zh: 代王丘為御史大夫。

translations.literal: He replaced Wang Qiu as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced Wang Qiu as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時司農卿陳思問引屬吏多小人，乾隱錢谷，尚隱按其違，贓累鉅萬，思問流死嶺南。

translations.literal: At that time Minister of Agriculture Chen Siwen employed many petty men among his subordinates who embezzled and concealed funds and grain. Shangyin investigated his violations; corruption accumulated to tens of thousands, and Siwen was exiled to die in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of agriculture Chen Siwen employed many corrupt subordinates who embezzled funds and grain. Shangyin investigated him, uncovered tens of thousands in graft, and Siwen was exiled to die in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 改尚隱太子詹事。

translations.literal: Shangyin was changed to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyin was reassigned as grand mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 不閱旬，進戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Within less than ten days he was advanced to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he was promoted to minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 前後更揚、益二州長史、東都留守，爵高邑伯。

translations.literal: Before and after he also served as Long History of Yang and Yi prefectures and Protector of the Eastern Capital, with the title Baron of Gaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as long history of Yang and Yi and as protector of the Eastern Capital, holding the title baron of Gaoyi.

sentences.zh: 開元二十八年，以太子賓客卒，年七十五，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Kaiyuan he died as Mentor of the Heir Apparent at age seventy-five and was given the posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 28 he died as mentor of the heir apparent at seventy-five, with the posthumous title Zhen.

sentences.zh: 尚隱三入御史府，輒繩惡吏，不以殘摯失名，所發當也，素議歸重。

translations.literal: Shangyin thrice entered the Censorate and always bound evil officials, not losing reputation through cruel severity; what he exposed was fitting, and public discussion returned weight to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyin entered the Censorate three times and always pursued corrupt officials without losing his reputation for cruelty. His charges were well founded, and public opinion held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 仕官未嘗以過謫，惟劾詆幸臣及坐小法左遷，復見用，以循吏終始雲。

translations.literal: In office he was never demoted for faults; only for impeaching and slandering favored ministers and for minor legal offenses was he demoted to the left, then seen and used again, ending as a model official throughout.
translations.idiomatic: He was never demoted for misconduct, only for impeaching favored ministers or minor legal infractions. Each time he was restored to office, and he ended his career as a model official.

sentences.zh: 自開元二十二年置京畿采訪處置等使，用中丞盧奐為之，尚隱以大夫不充使。

translations.literal: From the twenty-second year of Kaiyuan the Jingji Investigation and Disposition Commissioner and similar posts were established, with Vice Censor Lu Huan used for it; as chief censor Shangyin did not fill the commissioner post.
translations.idiomatic: From Kaiyuan 22 the court established the Jingji investigation and disposition commissioner, with vice censor Lu Huan in the role. As censor-in-chief, Shangyin did not hold that commission.

sentences.zh: 永泰以後，大夫王翊、崔渙、李涵、崔寧、盧杞乃為之。

translations.literal: After Yongtai, chief censors Wang Yi, Cui Huan, Li Han, Cui Ning, and Lu Qi then held it.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongtai, censors-in-chief Wang Yi, Cui Huan, Li Han, Cui Ning, and Lu Qi held the post.

sentences.zh: 解琬，魏州元城人。

translations.literal: Xie Wan was a native of Yuancheng in Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Wan was a native of Yuancheng in Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舉幽素科，中之，調新政尉。

translations.literal: He passed the Yousu examination category, was appointed Sheriff of Xinzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Yousu examination and was appointed sheriff of Xinzheng.

sentences.zh: 後自成都丞奏事稱旨，躐除監察御史，以喪免。

translations.literal: Later, reporting from his post as Chengdu Assistant Magistrate in a manner pleasing to the throne, he was leap-promoted to Investigating Censor and left office on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Later, memorializing from his post as assistant magistrate of Chengdu in a manner that pleased the throne, he was promoted directly to investigating censor and left office to mourn.

sentences.zh: 武後顧琬習邊事，迫追西撫羌夷，琬因乞終喪，後嘉許之，詔服除赴屯。

translations.literal: Empress Wu, seeing that Wan was versed in frontier affairs, urgently pursued him to pacify the Qiang and Yi in the west. Wan therefore begged to complete mourning; the Empress praised this and issued an edict that after mourning he should proceed to garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu, noting Wan's knowledge of frontier affairs, urgently recalled him to pacify the Qiang and Yi in the west. Wan asked to complete his mourning period, which the empress approved, and after mourning he was ordered to his post.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史，安撫烏質勒及十姓部落，以功擢御史中丞，兼北庭都護、西域安撫使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attending Censor, pacified Wuzhile and the ten-name tribes, and for merit was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief, concurrently Protector of Beiting and Commissioner for Pacification of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attending censor, pacified Wuzhile and the ten-name tribes, and for his merit was made vice censor-in-chief, concurrent protector of Beiting and commissioner for pacification of the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 琬與郭元振善，宗楚客惡之，左授滄州刺史。

translations.literal: Wan was on good terms with Guo Yuanzhen; Zong Chuke hated him and transferred him to the left as Prefect of Cang.
translations.idiomatic: Wan was close to Guo Yuanzhen. Zong Chuke resented him and had him transferred to prefect of Cang.

sentences.zh: 為政引大體，部人順附。

translations.literal: In governing he followed great principle, and the people of the prefecture submitted and attached themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He governed by broad principles, and the people of the prefecture willingly followed him.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，遷御史大夫，兼朔方行軍大總管。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Grand General of the Mobile Army of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong reign he was made censor-in-chief and concurrent grand general of the Shuofang mobile army.

sentences.zh: 前後乘邊積二十年，大抵務農習戰，多為長利，華虜安之。

translations.literal: Before and after he held the frontier for twenty years in all, generally devoting himself to agriculture and military training, achieving many lasting benefits, and both Chinese and barbarians were settled.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the frontier for twenty years in all, emphasizing farming and military training, achieving lasting benefits, and bringing peace to both Chinese and non-Chinese subjects.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，復為朔方軍大總管，分遣隨軍要籍官河陽丞張冠宗、肥鄉令韋景駿、普安令於處忠料三城兵，省其戍十萬人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyun he was again Grand General of the Shuofang Army, dispatching separately the army registry officials Heyang Assistant Magistrate Zhang Guanzong, Feixiang Magistrate Wei Jingjun, and Pu'an Magistrate Yu Chuzhong to assess the troops of three cities and reduce their garrison by one hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyun 2 he again became grand general of the Shuofang army. He sent registry officials Zhang Guanzong, Wei Jingjun, and Yu Chuzhong to assess troops in three cities and reduced the garrison by one hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 改右武衛大將軍，兼檢校晉州刺史、濟南縣男。

translations.literal: He was changed to General of the Right Martial Guards, concurrently Acting Prefect of Jin and Baron of Jinan County.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general of the right martial guards, concurrent acting prefect of Jin, and baron of Jinan County.

sentences.zh: 以老丐骸骨，不待報輒去，優詔以金紫光祿大夫聽致仕，準品給全祿，璽書勞問。

translations.literal: On account of age he begged to resign his bones; without awaiting reply he left. A gracious edict made him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and permitted retirement, granting full salary according to rank, with an imperial letter of consolation and inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire on account of old age and left without waiting for a reply. The court graciously permitted him to retire as grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal and purple ribbon, granted his full salary, and sent an imperial letter of consolation.

sentences.zh: 會吐番騷邊，復召授左散騎常侍，詔與虜定經界，因諧輯十姓降戶。

translations.literal: It happened that the Tibetans disturbed the border; he was again summoned and appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, with an edict to fix boundaries with the barbarians, and thereby harmoniously gathered the surrendered households of the ten-name tribes.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans raided the frontier, he was recalled as left regular attendant of the cavalry, ordered to fix boundaries with them, and successfully reconciled the surrendered households of the ten-name tribes.

sentences.zh: 琬建言吐蕃不可以信約，請調兵十萬屯秦、渭間，防遏其奸。

translations.literal: Wan memorialized that Tibet could not be trusted by treaty and requested one hundred thousand troops stationed between Qin and Wei to guard against their treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Wan memorialized that Tibet could not be trusted by treaty and asked for one hundred thousand troops stationed between Qin and Wei to guard against treachery.

sentences.zh: 是冬，吐蕃果入寇，為秦渭兵擊走之。

translations.literal: That winter Tibet indeed invaded, and was driven off by the Qin and Wei troops.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Tibet did invade and was driven off by the Qin and Wei troops.

sentences.zh: 俄復請老，不許，遷太子賓客。

translations.literal: Soon he again requested retirement; this was not permitted, and he was transferred to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to retire again, but the request was denied, and he was made mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 年八十餘，開元五年，終同州刺史。

translations.literal: At age more than eighty, in the fifth year of Kaiyuan, he died as Prefect of Tong.
translations.idiomatic: At more than eighty, he died in Kaiyuan 5 while serving as prefect of Tong.
